objectives: Map each phoneme to a letter.
Spell controlled /k/ CVC words with short vowels.
Repair spelling errors by locating the incorrect sound-letter mapping.
concepts: Encoding moves from spoken sounds to written letters.
CVC spelling depends on hearing all three phonemes.
Middle-vowel errors can change the word.

definitions.definition: Representing spoken sounds with written letters.
Separating a spoken word into its individual sounds.
Choosing the letter that represents each heard phoneme.

workedExamples: If cup is spelled cap, isolate and correct the middle /u/ sound.
commonMistakes: Confusing c and k at the beginning.
Writing from memory without saying the sounds.

conceptual: Identify each phoneme position in a CVC word.
application: Repair incorrect /k/ CVC spellings using sound evidence.
higherOrderThinking: Explain how a single vowel change creates a different spelling and word.
mixedReview: Combine sound segmentation with /k/ CVC encoding across short vowels.

formulaOrFactBank: CVC spelling = one written representation for each heard phoneme
mistakeBasedRevision: If spelling is wrong, say the word slowly and locate the sound that was mapped incorrectly.
weakTopicRevision: Repeat sound-box spelling for the weakest vowel contrast.

activities.name: Sound boxes
steps: Push one counter for each sound.
Choose a letter for each sound.

activities.name: Dictation repair
steps: Circle the incorrect mapping if present.

outcomes: Learner repairs vowel and initial-letter spelling errors.

questions.question: Which letter represents the first sound in “cat”?
Which letter represents the first sound in “kid”?
What is the middle sound in “cup”?
What is the last sound in “cop”?
A learner spells “cup” as “cap.” Which part needs checking?
What should you do before spelling “kid”?
options: Write the word from memory without saying it

questions.question: Which sequence is best for spelling a CVC word?
options: say → segment → map sounds to letters → reread
guess → write → skip sounds → move on
write first letter → guess the rest → stop

questions.question: Which pair changes only the middle vowel sound?
Why is rereading the spelled word useful?
options: It checks whether the letters represent the intended sounds
It removes the need to segment

questions.question: What is the main goal of this lesson?
options: Spell /k/ CVC words by segmenting sounds and mapping each sound to a letter
Memorize whole words without sound analysis
